expr: (list (let ((re (regexp-opt (list "a" "ab") t))) (list (string-match re "ab") (match-string 1 "ab"))) (let ((re (regexp-opt (list "ab") (quote words)))) (list (string-match re "x ab y") (match-end 0))))
note: THE ARGUMENT NOTHING IN s.el PASSES, measured so the freeze can say so with a number rather than an intention. Emacs answers ((0 "ab") (2 4)): PAREN `t' wraps the alternation in a CAPTURING group, so the whole match is also group 1 -- which SHIFTS every group number a caller's own regexp would have had -- and PAREN `words' wraps it in \\< ... \\> word boundaries, which are ZERO-WIDTH, so the match over "x ab y" is the word itself at 2..4 and what changes is that the same members would no longer match inside a longer word. Measured demand: the vendored s.el calls `regexp-opt' exactly once, at s.el:420 inside `s-replace-all', with ONE argument. THE DECISION, MADE: kg's `regexp-opt' takes STRINGS and nothing else, and a second argument is a named arity error (`wrong-number-of-arguments'), not an argument accepted and ignored -- the Phase 14 `intern' precedent, where an optional OBARRAY kg cannot honour is refused by name rather than silently dropped. kg answers `void-function' at this pin.
